links.outcome: Model performance under controlled missing, incoherent, invalid, imprecise and duplicate data at inference time
links.effect: Performance declined with increasing degradation, with largest losses when degradations occurred at inference time. Completeness, coherence and validity were the most detrimental dimensions.
links.quote: Model performance declined with increasing degradation, with the largest losses observed when degradations occurred at inference time.

links.outcome: Model robustness to perturbed or missing input data across five data quality dimensions
links.effect: Models adapted to training-time imperfections but remained sensitive to previously unseen degradations at deployment.
links.quote: Models adapted to training-time imperfections but remained sensitive to previously unseen degradations at deployment.

unlisted_practices: Training models on degraded data to improve robustness to training-time data quality imperfections

screen.reason: Evaluates the robustness of healthcare ML models under simulated data quality degradation across MIMIC-IV datasets, identifying failure modes but not evaluating a specific deployment practice/safeguard intervention.
